status: Two separate post-hoc robustness/falsification designs selected after observing the originally preregistered nine-path experiment; not independent blind confirmation
core_scenario: Original substantial; original monthly labor, wage, matching, capital and ideas equations unchanged
scope: Only change the exogenous time-shape of m(t) and d(t) between 2026.5 and 2030. All exogenous technology paths identical in 2024-2026.5 and at 2030; never rewrite source.

control_1.method: Define s=(t-2026.5)/3.5; for 2026.5<t<2030 replace original logistic m(t),d(t) by evaluating both at t_eff=2026.5+3.5*(s+alpha*s*(1-s)); outside this period use original m,d exactly. a(t), psi,rho,mu,theta_H identical.
control_1.hypothesis: frontloaded alpha=+0.75 gives lower 2030 AI-sensitive unemployment than late alpha=-0.75, >0.05 percentage-point difference
control_1.limitation: Changes endpoint derivatives, so differences may reflect current 2030 adoption velocity as well as history

control_2.method: Let s=(t-2026.5)/3.5; for 2026.5<t<2030 replace original m(t),d(t) with values at t_eff=2026.5+3.5*(s+alpha*s^2*(1-s)^2). At both s=0,1, dt_eff/dt=1 for all alpha. Before 2026.5 and at and after 2030, use original path. a and remaining assumptions unchanged.
control_2.hypothesis: frontloaded alpha=+2.5 yields 2030 cognitive unemployment at least 0.05 pp below alpha=-2.5 despite equal endpoint levels AND slopes
control_2.limitation: Time-warp is a controlled alternative exogenous adoption path, not the original paper's Equation (8) logistic trajectory

tests: same m,d,a and initial employment stocks at 2024 and 2026.5
original source substantial reappears at alpha zero
same endpoint m,d slope only in control_2
disclaimer: All results concern conditional U.S. model dynamics. Not a policy lever, adoption forecast, or inference about firms' actual hiring reactions.
